question: Within five already source-validated periodic D4 red-X fixtures, which action/future-fault histories can even alter an unconditional complete next-first law at matched first record and final support through second-measurement dephasing?
role: Bounded necessary-condition screen before another expensive exact Born-law matrix; no physical caller integration or schedule sampling
source_basis: Jing Appendix A.2/A.4 red-X conjugated star and ideal local charge projectors
J6L/J6M periodic source geometry, triangle-vacuum commutator and common orbit

model.geometry_state: Pinned periodic L=2, 108-qubit J6M triangle-vacuum orbit; ideal source red-X faults, source star projectors and no readout noise
model.first_record: The same complete eligible 24-site binary first public record is conditioned on both branches; no first outcomes are generated in this structural screen
model.second_record: For each nonempty in-support public red-X correction subset, all flux-free stars on its actual residual sector are the full second measurement set; no selected-site surrogate
model.future_record: After zero or one private physical red-X fault drawn from that fixture's original edge set, all flux-free stars on the final support are the complete next-first measurement set
model.matched_history: Group histories by identical initial geometry and final red-X support. Compare distinct public corrections only, and retain action/future-fault labels privately in this diagnostic; do not infer causal action effects from differently timed faults
model.commutation: For Q_s(E)=X_E A_s X_E=sign Z_z A_s, compute pair commutator on the triangle-vacuum orbit as the J6M star-pair Z mask (vacuum-trivial) times (-1)^(f_s dot z_t + f_t dot z_s). A nonzero binary exponent for an eligible second/next pair is a necessary opening for second-measurement dephasing to alter the marginalized next law, not evidence that it actually does
model.independent_unit_uncertainty: One exact finite graph and common orbit, five fixed physical support fixtures; Boolean structural classifications have no sampling interval and cannot establish a general no-go

matrix.actions: Every nonempty subset of the fixture's physical edges, with the complete actual-sector second measurement set
matrix.future_faults: None or exactly one edge from the same fixture, producing a complete actual-sector next-first measurement set
matrix.pair_rule: Two histories with identical initial geometry and final support but distinct public correction subsets. Classify each branch by presence/absence of any eligible second-versus-next star anticommutator, then count pairs where at least one branch has such a witness; do not call an anticommutator sufficient for a nonzero exact total variation
controls: Same-sector eligible star pairs commute on the triangle-vacuum orbit
Every eligible set matches the public flux-free sites
J7C registered branch A/B appears as an identical-final-support pair and its prior exact null remains unaltered
Full source and frozen-caller hashes match before and after

competing_outcomes.structural_opening: At least one support-matched pair has a second/next anticommutator; rank only pre-existing fixtures by minimum edge count, number of noncommuting branches and then lexicographic keys for a separately registered exact probability test
competing_outcomes.finite_commuting_no_go: No pair in this five-fixture bounded matrix has such a witness; record only a finite necessary-condition no-go and stop larger Born enumeration on these fixtures
competing_outcomes.censored: Any source, flux eligibility, same-sector commutation, orbit or cap check fails; do not infer a structural candidate

acceptance: All eight input pins pass before and after
Exactly the five frozen fixture supports are screened without adding topology or changing the J7C result
Full actual-sector eligible sets and same-sector commuting controls pass, and a matched-support pair includes J7C A/B
The output records full branch and pair counts and whether a structural opening exists; a witness is not promoted to a nonzero public-law difference
No caller invocation/mutation, dependency installation, stochastic history, schedule arm or bootstrap
stop_rule: Stop at any pin, geometry, sector, commutation, coverage or budget failure. No exact Born probability enumeration, enlarged graph, full caller integration, JIT risk or threshold inference in this tick; if a structural opening survives, preregister the smallest exact follow-up before evaluating it.
